description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/backend.rs:35-54

```rust
fn create_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>(
    &self,
    caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
    account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
    create_id: &str,
    obj: O,
) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = Result<(jmap_types::Id, O), BackendSetError<Self::Error>>>
       + Send;
```

with rustdoc invariant:

> The returned `O` MUST have its `id` field set to the server-assigned
> `Id` returned as the first element of the tuple. The handler relies
> on this to populate the `created` response map per RFC 8620 §5.3 ...

This is a hand-written invariant that:

1. **Is unenforceable at the type level.** Nothing in the Rust type
   system links the `Id` element of the tuple to the `id` field of
   the `O` value. A backend implementor who reads this rustdoc and
   forgets — or misreads — produces a wire-incorrect response. The
   handler at `principal.rs:117-123` blindly serializes
   `created_obj` and inserts the result into the `created` response
   map without any consistency check.

2. **Is already violated by the in-tree MockBackend.** lib.rs:341-346
   admits this in a code comment:

   ```rust
   // INVARIANT GAP: the returned `obj` retains whatever placeholder
   // id was passed in by the caller — it is NOT patched to
   // \"mock-id-1\". This violates the SharingBackend::create_object
   // invariant ...
   Ok((Id::from(\"mock-id-1\"), obj))
   ```

   A documented in-tree violation by a test fixture is a strong
   signal that downstream backend implementors will hit the same
   gap. The mitigation \"use MemoryBackend for tests that require a
   correct create response\" is itself a defensive-coding burden
   on downstream contributors.

3. **Has a known safer shape.** Either:
   - Return just the `Id` and let the handler call `get_objects`
     to re-fetch the canonical-stored object. Adds one read per
     create but removes the invariant.
   - Return a thin newtype `Created<O>` whose constructor takes
     `(Id, O)` and writes the Id into `O.id` automatically. The
     handler can only get an O whose id is consistent.
   - Make the handler itself patch `O.id = new_id` after the
     backend call. Backend impls then need not maintain the
     invariant.

What goes wrong for callers when this stays as-is: a downstream
SharingBackend implementor reads only the trait, returns the original
client-supplied `obj` (which the handler at `principal.rs:91-100`
populates with `\"placeholder\"` if missing), and ships a backend
where every `Principal/set create` response echoes the literal string
\"placeholder\" as the `id` field. The wire breakage is silent —
no error, just incorrect JMAP responses. Detectable only by
end-to-end test, not by `cargo test` of the backend alone.

Cross-references: JMAP-3t94.4 (no test coverage for unknown-account
on /set) does not cover this; this is a separate defensive-coding
gap that would benefit from an in-tree integration test asserting
the invariant against every shipped SharingBackend impl.
notes:
Three-part fix:
1. backend.rs: tightened SharingBackend::create_object rustdoc with strong language explicitly calling out the unenforceable-at-the-type-level nature, the silent wire-bug failure mode, the canonical implementation pattern (serialize/mutate-id/deserialize round-trip), and bd:JMAP-3t94.17 tracking.
2. lib.rs MockBackend: removed the INVARIANT GAP code-comment escape hatch; the mock now serializes obj, patches id field, deserializes back — matching the canonical jmap-mail-server MemoryBackend pattern.
3. Regression tests:
   - src/memory.rs::tests::create_object_returned_o_carries_server_assigned_id
   - src/lib.rs::tests::mock_backend_create_object_returned_o_carries_server_id
Both serialize the stored object and assert val["id"] == tuple Id.

Workspace-architectural follow-up deferred: the handler-side defensive patch (option 3 from the bead) would touch the canonical jmap-mail-server handler. Tracked separately if/when motivated.
title: SharingBackend::create_object id-on-O invariant is unenforceable; MockBackend in same crate violates it silently
